content: ACES is an acronym for a category of nutritional supplements that combine antioxidants, specifically beta-carotene (or other carotenoids) for (pro)vitamin A, vitamin C, vitamin E, and selenium. These supplements are available in various formulations, differing in the concentration, specific components, sources, and ratios of their ingredients, depending on the manufacturer. They are typically offered in tablet or capsule form. Beta-carotene, one of over 600 known carotenoids, is the most commonly used source of vitamin A activity in ACES formulations. For vitamin C activity, ascorbic acid and its derivatives, such as ascorbates, are the standard ingredients. The vitamin E content in these supplements often varies and may include forms such as dl-alpha-tocopheryl acetate (all-rac-alpha-tocopheryl acetate), d-alpha-tocopheryl acetate, d-alpha-tocopheryl succinate, or d-alpha-tocopherol. Selenium, another key component, is provided in different forms, including selenate, selenium-enriched nutritional yeast, and organic selenium compounds like L-selenomethionine and L-selenium-methylselenocysteine, with variations depending on the manufacturer. More recent ACES formulations have incorporated mixed natural carotenoid sources, which may include other carotenoids such as zeaxanthin, alpha-carotene, cryptoxanthin, lutein, and lycopene. Similarly, mixed tocopherols, containing varying proportions of R,R,R-alpha-tocopherol, R,R,R-beta-tocopherol, R,R,R-gamma-tocopherol, and R,R,R-delta-tocopherol, are also used as sources of vitamin E in some formulations. During the 1980s, ACES supplements gained popularity due to increased commercial growth and public awareness. Over time, these formulations have evolved, often incorporating small amounts of additional antioxidants such as lipoic acid, pycnogenol, coenzyme Q-10, and N-acetylcysteine, as well as other nutrients. These expanded formulations are sometimes marketed as super antioxidants or under proprietary trade names, with their specific compositions varying by manufacturer. Typical ACES formulations contain approximately 10,000 to 25,000 IU of carotenoids, 250 mg to 1,000 mg of vitamin C, 200 to 400 IU of alpha-tocopherol, and 50 mcg to 200 mcg of selenium per serving, which usually consists of one to three tablets or capsules. In more recent antioxidant formulations, additional nutrients may also be included.
